title: Bellbird Bay Rising
premise: Felix Nystrom, a pastry chef drowning in café debt, and Marisol Vega, the bank officer processing his foreclosure, are anonymously assigned to each other through a coastal town's centennial pen-pal project meant to heal old grudges. Writing under pseudonyms, they confess fears neither can voice in person — while by day, Felix and Marisol spar as adversaries, and Marisol hides that her bank's parent company plans to raze Bellbird Bay's harbor district, her own childhood home included. As the letters deepen into love, Felix discovers his correspondent is the woman destroying him, forcing both to choose between duty and truth. In the end they expose the redevelopment scheme at the centennial gala, save the harbor, and forgive themselves enough to meet — unmasked — on the pier where the first letter was posted.
about_author: Orsen Okonkwo is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters recovered from coastal lighthouse stations before turning to fiction. He writes romances about people who mistake duty for destiny, from a houseboat studio he shares with an opinionated kelpie-cross dog.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A final notice arrives at the café on the morning of the town's pen-pal project launch; Felix signs up on a dare from his barista, insisting hearts are trainable muscles. Emotional beat: bravado masking terror of loss.

chapters.title: The Officer and the Order
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol receives Felix's foreclosure file and, recognizing the café where she once ate birthday cake, requests the assignment anyway — then signs up for the pen-pal project her grandmother helped found. Emotional beat: guilt she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Enemies at the Counter
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marisol delivers the default warning in person; Felix throws her out with a box of ruined éclairs. That night, both receive their anonymous assignments. Emotional beat: fury curdling into curiosity.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Alternating letters. 'Kestrel' (Marisol) and 'Anchor' (Felix) trade first guarded letters about what they'd save from a fire. By day they avoid each other at the harbor market. Emotional beat: unexpected recognition between strangers.

chapters.title: Proof in the Proofing Box
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A failed croissant batch and a visit from his estranged mother, who wants the café sold to cover her own debts. He writes Anchor's confession about inherited failure. Emotional beat: shame becoming honesty on paper.

chapters.title: The Harbor File
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finds a confidential memo: the parent bank plans a marina resort over the harbor district. Her grandmother's cottage sits in the footprint. She says nothing. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: Salt and Sugar
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Forced together by the centennial committee, Felix and Marisol co-judge the baking contest; their rivalry sparks something warmer mid-argument. That night both letters turn flirtatious. Emotional beat: the two lives beginning to bleed together.

chapters.title: What Kestrel Won't Say
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Kestrel's letter confesses complicity in 'an act that will hurt someone innocent.' Marisol nearly tells Felix the truth at his counter but the bank's regional director appears, watching. Emotional beat: cowardice she can't forgive in herself.

chapters.title: Anchor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix audits his finances and realizes only a miracle — or the bank — can save the café. He writes to Kestrel about wanting to hate someone so he doesn't hate himself. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strength.

chapters.title: Rain on the Pier
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm strands Felix and Marisol under the pier awning; a near-kiss is interrupted by her ringing phone — the bank. Later, both letters admit wanting to meet. Emotional beat: longing outrunning loyalty.

chapters.title: The Deadline Clause
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The director gives Marisol a choice: finalize Felix's foreclosure by month's end or lose her job — the job paying her grandmother's care bills. She signs. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice, Hand-Delivered
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Marisol serves Felix the final notice; he calls her every cruel thing he's ever thought. Alone, he writes Kestrel that he's fallen for someone he can't have. Emotional beat: heartbreak on both sides of one door.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Sorting her grandmother's attic, Marisol finds decades of pen-pal letters — including one from Felix's late father, and proof the original project once stopped a developer cold. Emotional beat: inheritance as instruction.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix notices Kestrel's phrasing echoes Marisol's at the counter — 'the heart is a ledger, not a muscle.' He tests her with a planted phrase. She responds to it in the next letter. Emotional beat: suspicion arriving like a cold tide.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Felix confronts Marisol at the postbox at midnight; she admits everything — the letters, the memo, the signed foreclosure. He walks away. Both write final, unsent letters. Emotional beat: betrayal and the mirror it holds up.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Split POV. Felix bakes his father's abandoned signature loaf and forgives his mother; Marisol visits her grandmother and admits her silence. Each realizes the enemy was never only the other. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness as the true climax's groundwork.

chapters.title: The Centennial Gala
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the gala, the bank unveils the marina resort. Marisol takes the stage with her grandmother's letters and the confidential memo, publicly resigning. Emotional beat: truth as an act of loyalty.

chapters.title: Anchor, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix, in the crowd, holds up his own unsent final letter and reads it aloud — forgiving her in front of the town. The crowd, many of them harbor families, turns against the development. Emotional beat: love declared against consequence.

chapters.title: The Vote at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The town council, armed with the historical letters proving the project's original covenant, votes down the rezoning; the bank withdraws. Felix's foreclosure is voided. Emotional beat: survival won collectively, not alone.

chapters.title: What the Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Rebuilding the café with volunteer hands, Felix admits to his barista that the heart isn't containable at all — it just needed honest training. Emotional beat: joy after ruin.

chapters.title: The Pier at First Light
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marisol leaves a letter in the old postbox: 'Meet me where it started, no pseudonyms.' Felix finds her at sunrise; their first kiss is witnessed only by bellbirds. Emotional beat: arrival, at last, without masks.

chapters.title: Bellbird Bay Rising
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating. One year later: the café thrives, the harbor district is a protected heritage quarter, and the pen-pal project continues with a new generation. Marisol and Felix co-write the project's founding letter. Emotional beat: love and town, risen together.
